title: Experimentation runtime: A/B testing framework and statistical guardrails for model versions
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Build an end-to-end A/B testing framework for model versions that supports controlled exposure, statistically sound stopping rules, shadow traffic evaluation, and automated rollback hooks. Objective: enable Product and ML teams to run short- and medium-duration experiments on text-generation and embedding endpoints with clear guardrails for latency, safety, and quality. Scope includes experiment configuration schema, backend bucketing and routing, sequential statistical checks, Console UX for experiment creation/monitoring, and automated rollback policies. Out of scope: complete offline evaluation tooling (will integrate with existing eval pipelines) and multi-armed bandit adaptive allocation for this initial phase.
acceptance_criteria: API to create experiments with configurable exposure percent, bucketing seed, primary/secondary metrics, and minimum duration
Routing layer can split traffic deterministically per request and apply shadow mirror without affecting production response
Statistical engine runs sequential checks and emits decision recommendations (continue/stop/rollback) according to configured alpha and power settings
Console UI surfaces experiment status, real-time metric deltas, CI/CIs, and a one-click rollback action tied to the rollout policy
Alerts trigger when primary or guardrail metrics breach thresholds during an active experiment
Automated rollback executes safely: drains new model traffic, falls back to nominated baseline, and creates an incident ticket with telemetry
plan_steps: Design: finalize experiment config schema (exposure, hypothesis, power, MDE, alpha, metrics, stratification keys)
Eng: implement deterministic bucketing in routing layer (request-level hash, consistent bucketing across retries)
Eng: add shadow traffic mirror pipeline for offline comparison without altering live responses
Stats: implement sequential testing module with alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming style) and optional Bayesian posterior checks
Console: experiment creation form and monitoring dashboard with % exposure controls and rollout timeline visualization
Observability: add experiment tags to traces/metrics, per-model time series, and pre-built dashboards
Safety: implement guardrail checks (hallucination signal, policy violations, latency P95) and circuit-breaker action
QA: run canary with synthetic traffic and small customer pilot, validate data integrity and bucketing stability
Release: staged rollout of experimentation API behind feature flag; enable for internal teams first
metrics: primary_metric: task success rate (pass@k or rubric-based binary pass) or user-reported acceptance
secondary_metrics: generation latency P50/P95, cost per token
safety_guardrails: policy-violation-rate, hallucination proxy (confidence drop / hallucination-detect model)
business_metrics: CTR, containment rate for support flows
exposure_metrics: percent of requests routed to variant, unique users exposed
stat_tests: p-value, confidence interval, posterior probability of improvement/degradation
rollout_policy: Default rollout pattern: 1% (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) -> 100% (rolling). Each step requires: minimum sample size or minimum time window (whichever is larger), no critical guardrail breach, and no statistically significant degradation. Statistical checks: sequential alpha-spending with overall alpha=0.01 by default; statistical power target 0.8 and default MDE configurable per metric. Rollback triggers: (a) any safety_guardrail breaches above configured threshold for >2 consecutive windows, (b) primary metric degradation beyond MDE with p<0.01, or (c) posterior probability of harm >0.95. Rollback action: immediate revert to baseline variant and create incident with diagnostic bundle.
risk_assessment: Risks: biased bucketing causing uneven customer exposure (mitigation: deterministic hashing and holdout tests), p-hacking from too-frequent manual checks (mitigation: default sequential testing and audit logs), false positives on safety proxies (mitigation: require sustained breach over multiple windows and correlate signals), data loss in experiment tagging (mitigation: integrity checks and replayable logs). High-severity risk: rollback automation accidentally flips unrelated routing (mitigation: scope rollback to experiment ID and model namespace; add safety review gate for cross-service rollbacks).
